item.title: UN Adopts Revolutionary Map Projection System
item.description:
UN Adopts Revolutionary New World Map to Correct Geographic Proportions

A Historic Step Toward Accurate Global Representation

In a landmark decision that challenges over four centuries of cartographic convention, the United Nations has officially adopted a new map projection system designed to accurately represent the true proportions of countries and continents across the globe. This significant shift moves away from the widely-used Mercator projection, which has dominated world maps since its introduction in 1569 and has long been criticized for distorting the relative sizes of nations, particularly affecting how we perceive countries in the Global South.

item.title: Ford Plants Giant Lake Ontario Sign
item.description:
Ford Plants Giant Lake Ontario Sign

Ontario Premier Doug Ford answered President Trump’s executive order renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America” by unveiling a huge bilingual blue billboard at Fifty Point Conservation Area near Hamilton. The object is not a press release and not a matching decree. It is a physical sign on Canadian ground, large enough to read from the water, planted where a shoreline crowd and a camera phone can both see it. The English face reads “Lake Ontario Now and Always.” The French face reads “Lac Ontario - Aujourd’hui et pour toujours.” Together they are one claim in Canada’s two official languages: the lake already has a name, and that name is not up for a presidential rewrite.

item.title: Ford Unveils Two-Story Name Rebuke
item.description:
Ford Unveils Two-Story Name Rebuke

Ontario Premier Doug Ford answered President Donald Trump’s Thursday order renaming Lake Ontario “Lake America” by unveiling a shoreline billboard Saturday: “Lake Ontario. Now and Always.” The reply was not a diplomatic note and not a matching decree. It was a physical object on Canadian ground, large enough to read as architecture, planted where the water and the cameras could not miss it. CBS said the blue display also reads in French “Lac Ontario - Aujourd’hui et pour toujours” at Fifty Point Conservation Area. Wearing a Team Canada soccer jersey, Ford posed near Grimsby.

item.title: Lee Know Funds Nepal Flood Relief
item.description:
Lee Know Funds Nepal Flood Relief

JYP Entertainment said Aug. 30 that Stray Kids member Lee Know donated 100 million won (~$75,000) to World Vision for emergency relief after catastrophic Nepal-Tibet flash floods. The announcement is brief, as agency statements about an idol’s private giving usually are. The facts inside it are not. The gift, delivered Aug. 28, is earmarked for food, nutrition, temporary housing, and safe water and sanitation for children and families hit by the disaster. It arrives while Nepal and Tibet still search for thousands missing after glacier-triggered floods killed hundreds along the border.

item.title: Deadly Trump-Shaped Pills Spark Dutch Alert
item.description:
Deadly Trump-Shaped Pills Spark Dutch Alert

A novelty stamp and a delayed poison

The Dutch have spent decades treating the night-time drug market as something that can be watched rather than wished away. That culture of surveillance, built around walk-in testing rooms and a national early-warning network, is why a handful of odd-looking tablets can still move a government institute to its highest public alarm. This month they did.

The Trimbos Institute, the Netherlands’ centre for mental health and addiction, issued a national Red Alert after testers found two-tone ecstasy tablets molded like President Donald Trump’s head, with “NL” and “Trump” stamped across a break line on the back. Several pills were turned in at Dutch testing centers in August. The Netherlands Forensic Institute analyzed one as well. The chemistry, not the caricature, is what triggered the alarm: labs found a very high dose of PMMA, a slower-acting MDMA analog that often lacks the expected buzz, so users may take another pill and overdose.

item.title: Iceland's Knife-Edge EU Vote Closes
item.description:
Iceland’s Knife-Edge EU Vote Closes

Icelanders voted Saturday on whether to reopen European Union accession talks, 13 years after Reykjavik froze a 2009 application. Polls closed at 10 p.m. GMT with the race too close to call. A Friday Gallup survey showed a slight No lead after earlier Yes edges. The island has a habit of making large decisions look small until they are not. This one will not resolve in a single television graphic.

item.title: White House Aide Bets On Speeches
item.description:
White House Aide Bets On Speeches

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Friday ordered former White House teleprompter operator Gabriel Perez to pay $172,539 for using advance copies of President Trump’s speeches to bet on Kalshi “mention markets,” contracts that pay if the president utters specific words or phrases. The number is precise because the conduct was. Perez did not have an opinion about the news. He had the script.
